hints: Notice the weight of the $2.4 \text{ kg}$ sign acts vertically down from its centre, which is halfway down the $0.86 \text{ m}$ side.
The sign is tilted $15^{\circ}$ to the vertical, so the horizontal distance from the hinge to the centre is $0.43 \sin 15^{\circ}$ in $\text{m}$.
Calculate $W = mg$ and then use moment $= W$ times that horizontal perpendicular distance.
walkthrough: Weight acts at the centre of mass of the uniform sign, $0.86/2 = 0.43 \text{ m}$ measured along the sign from the hinge.
Weight is $W = mg = 2.4 \times 9.81 \approx 23.5 \text{ N}$ acting vertically downwards.
Because the sign is at $15^{\circ}$ to the vertical, the horizontal perpendicular distance from the hinge to the vertical line through the centre is $d = 0.43 \sin 15^{\circ}$.
Moment about hinge $= Wd \approx 23.5 \times 0.111 \approx 2.6 \text{ N m}$ with units of $\text{N m}$.

options.A: Weight times perpendicular distance gives about $2.6 \text{ N m}$ clockwise about the hinge.
options.B: This is too large and results from an error in the distance from the hinge to the line of action of the weight.
options.C: This is twice the correct value because it uses the full $0.86 \text{ m}$ length instead of the $0.43 \text{ m}$ distance to the centre of mass.
options.D: This ignores the $\sin 15^{\circ}$ factor and uses $W$ times $0.43 \text{ m}$ directly, as if the sign were horizontal.
